happened: On March 21, 2025, the SBA announced a reorganization that would cut about 43 percent of its workforce, roughly 2,700 of 6,500 jobs, by ending "non-mission-critical positions and consolidating functions." The agency said its loan guarantee and disaster programs would not be affected. Congress later lowered the SBA's main operating budget from $361.2 million in fiscal 2024 to $323.1 million in fiscal 2026.

It also updated its fraud penalty rules (March 2026) and its Do Not Pay data matching (September 2026).

A 2022 SBA rule, before this administration, had already removed the religious limit for its 7(a), 504 and microloan business loans (see ch25-018).
